CRITICAL BUG FOUND & FIXED: POST /api/families/members/{id}/credentials returned 500 DuplicateKeyError on the SECOND child user creation per environment because the insert set `email: None` and the `users.email` unique index is `sparse=True` (sparse indexes still index explicit null values). Fix applied at server.py line 1418: OMIT the `email` field from the insert doc for child accounts so sparse skips them. Verified via retest (Priya credentialed after Anaya had already been credentialed in the same run). All 14 pytest cases still pass after the fix.
action_items: Review the small MongoDB-null-email fix applied in server.py set_member_credentials (line 1418): omitted `email` field on new child user insert to prevent DuplicateKeyError on 2nd child. If E1 prefers a schema-consistent fix, replace the sparse index with a partial-filter index: `users.create_index('email', unique=True, partialFilterExpression={'email': {'$type':'string'}})` and drop the old one at startup — currently the sparse index still keeps working because we simply don't include the field for child users.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: `users.email` unique index is declared with sparse=True, but a document explicitly set to `email: null` IS indexed by sparse (only *missing* fields are skipped). This is a subtle Mongo footgun. Fix by omitting the field OR migrating to a partial-filter unique index. Applied the 'omit the field' fix.

rca_of_issue: BUG: POST /api/families/members/{id}/credentials returned 500 on the 2nd child user creation per Mongo database. Reproduction (before fix): (a) as admin, credential ONE pending member (e.g. Anaya) with any username+PIN — success. (b) as admin, credential ANOTHER pending member (e.g. Priya) with any username+PIN — 500 Internal Server Error. Backend log: `pymongo.errors.DuplicateKeyError: E11000 duplicate key error collection: test_database.users index: email_1 dup key: { email: null }`. ROOT CAUSE: server.py line 1420 (before fix) inserted `email: None` into `db.users` for every new child user; the `users.email` unique index is `sparse=True`, but sparse indexes ONLY skip documents where the field is MISSING — an explicit `email: null` IS indexed as null, and only one such doc is allowed under a unique index. So the second child insert always collides. FIX: drop `email: None` from the insert doc; sparse then skips the doc and multiple email-less child users co-exist safely. Reproduction after fix: created Priya login after Anaya login, no 500. All pytest tests still green. MITIGATION for E1: consider migrating to a partialFilterExpression unique index for extra robustness.
